correctness.rationale: The specified basis brackets are the semidirect product of integral sl₂ plus the scalar torus with its defining module, with alternating brackets retained after reduction. An independent exact Chevalley–Eilenberg reconstruction checked Jacobi and all five consecutive products. The unit and 2-factor counts in the six integer Smith forms were respectively (5,27,54,51,22,3) and (1,3,6,9,8,3), with no other nonzero factors. The ranks (6,30,60,60,30,6) give rational acyclicity at all degrees, including the ends. In each degree the kernel in the preceding cokernel has quotient the free image of the next differential, so the integral cohomology is precisely the preceding cokernel's torsion. The finite free alternating complex base-changes to any field: the Smith 2's vanish exactly in characteristic two, yielding (1,4,9,15,17,11,3); degrees beyond six are zero. In characteristic two h+t is central. The alternating form supported on the x,y wedge is invariant under the complement spanned by e,f,h,t, whose action on span(x,y) is trace zero in this characteristic. Thus its h+t-valued cochain is closed. No [x,G(y)] or [y,G(x)] has a t-component, and [x,y]=0 before deformation, so the cochain is not exact. It kills its own image in the inputs, which makes the quadratic Jacobi term zero over every field of characteristic two. A nonzero parameter adds the independent h+t direction to the original derived span of h,x,y.

value.rationale: The defining irreducible module and full scalar torus are natural inputs from the characteristic-zero rigidity theorem. The exact calculation identifies the sole bad prime and its complete elementary 2-torsion profile, rather than inferring modular information from rational rigidity. The exhibited deformation distinguishes the bad prime geometrically by a jump in the dimension of the derived algebra. The data can be used to study which characteristic-zero rigidity phenomena survive reduction on this integral model.
residual_risks: This exact witness and profile do not classify other lattices or all modular deformation directions.
